benefits.name: Age Pension
benefits.summary: A fortnightly pension for people 67 or older who pass the income and assets tests.
benefits.eligibility_text: Age 67 or older; within the income and assets test limits; Australian resident, normally for at least 10 years.
benefits.value_text: Up to $1,237.70 a fortnight single, or $933.00 each for a couple ($1,866.00 combined), including Pension Supplement and Energy Supplement
benefits.how_to_claim: Claim online through myGov (Centrelink online account) or at a service centre.
benefits.notes: Max annual = single fortnightly x 26. Basic rate alone $1,135.40 single / $855.90 each couple. Assets test free area from 1 Jul 2026: $333,000 single homeowner / $600,000 non-homeowner; $499,000 / $766,000 couple (guides.dss.gov.au 4/10/3). Income free area $5,876 pa single, $5,148 pa each couple. Services Australia rate page still showed older $1,178.70 when fetched. Eligibility from servicesaustralia.gov.au/age-pension.

benefits.name: Pension Supplement
benefits.summary: An extra amount paid with your pension to help with everyday costs such as bills.
benefits.eligibility_text: Paid automatically with Age Pension, Carer Payment and other pensions.
benefits.value_text: Up to $88.20 a fortnight single, $66.50 each for a couple (minimum $47.50 single / $35.80 each)
benefits.how_to_claim: Paid automatically with your pension; no separate claim.
benefits.notes: Already included in the Age Pension maximum; max_annual_value left null to avoid double counting.

benefits.name: Energy Supplement (Commonwealth Seniors Health Card holders)
benefits.summary: A quarterly payment to help with energy costs for some CSHC holders who got their card before 20 March 2017.
benefits.eligibility_text: Commonwealth Seniors Health Card holders who were already getting it; closed to new CSHC holders from 20 March 2017. Pensioners get it inside their pension.
benefits.value_text: $366.60 a year single ($91.65 a quarter), $275.60 a year each for a couple
benefits.value_period: Current annual rate (DSS guide reviewed 2 Jan 2026)
benefits.how_to_claim: Paid automatically each quarter if you are eligible.
benefits.notes: Pension recipients receive $14.10 a fortnight single / $10.60 each couple inside the pension. DVA CLIK lists quarterly payment for quarter to 19/12/2026 at $91.65 single / $68.90 partnered.

benefits.name: Work Bonus
benefits.summary: Lets pensioners earn some work income without it reducing their pension.
benefits.eligibility_text: Pensioners over Age Pension age who receive a pension (also applies to DVA pensions).
benefits.value_text: First $300 a fortnight of work income is not counted; unused amounts build up to a balance of $11,800
benefits.how_to_claim: Applied automatically when you report your employment income to Centrelink.
benefits.notes: Not a cash payment; value depends on earnings.

benefits.name: Rent Assistance
benefits.summary: Extra money paid with your pension if you pay private rent or certain other housing costs.
benefits.eligibility_text: People getting an income support payment such as Age Pension who pay rent above the threshold (not public housing).
benefits.value_text: Up to $223.80 a fortnight single ($149.20 if sharing), $211.00 a fortnight combined for a couple; 75c for every $1 of rent above $157.80 (single) / $255.80 (couple)
benefits.how_to_claim: Tell Centrelink your rent details when you claim your pension or through your online account.
benefits.notes: Max annual = single max x 26. Services Australia page still showed older $215.40 rate when fetched.

benefits.name: Remote Area Allowance
benefits.summary: A small extra payment if you live in a remote part of Australia and get an income support payment.
benefits.eligibility_text: Income support recipients living in a designated remote area (tax zone A or special areas).
benefits.value_text: $18.20 a fortnight single, $15.60 each for a couple
benefits.how_to_claim: Usually added automatically when Centrelink has your remote address.
benefits.notes: Remote-area definition not on the fetched page.

benefits.name: Pensioner Concession Card
benefits.summary: A card for pensioners that gives cheaper medicines and health care and unlocks state, council and business discounts.
benefits.eligibility_text: Given to people who get certain Centrelink payments, including Age Pension.
benefits.value_text: Cheaper PBS medicines, bulk-billing incentives and access to many state and private concessions
benefits.how_to_claim: Issued automatically when you are granted a qualifying pension.
benefits.notes: Laminated cards issued from December 2025; old and new both valid.

benefits.name: Commonwealth Seniors Health Card
benefits.summary: A card for self-funded retirees of pension age that gives cheaper medicines and some concessions.
benefits.eligibility_text: Age Pension age or older, meet residence rules, not getting a Centrelink/DVA income support payment, and income under the limit (no assets test).
benefits.value_text: Income limits: under $101,105 a year single, $161,768 a year combined for a couple ($202,210 if separated by illness)
benefits.value_period: Current limits shown on Services Australia
benefits.how_to_claim: Apply through your Centrelink online account via myGov.
benefits.notes: Account-based income streams are deemed. Benefits: PBS concession rate, PBS Safety Net, bulk-billing incentives, Extended Medicare Safety Net concessional threshold, discretionary state/private concessions (guides.dss.gov.au 3/9/3/20).

benefits.name: Home Equity Access Scheme
benefits.summary: A government loan against your home that tops up your income with fortnightly payments or lump sums.
benefits.eligibility_text: Age Pension age (or partner of someone who is); qualify for Age Pension, DSP or Carer Payment (need not be paid it); own Australian real estate as security with adequate insurance; not bankrupt.
benefits.value_text: Pension plus loan up to 150% of the maximum pension rate; lump-sum advances up to 50% of the annual maximum pension rate (max 2 per 26 fortnights); interest 3.95% a year compounding fortnightly; no negative equity guarantee
benefits.value_period: Interest rate 3.95% (from 1 Jan 2022, still current per DSS guide)
benefits.how_to_claim: Apply through Centrelink; for an existing loan use form D9390 for an advance.
benefits.notes: Formerly the Pension Loans Scheme. A loan, not a grant. Interest rate from guides.dss.gov.au 3/4/5/45; advance rules from servicesaustralia.gov.au/home-equity-access-scheme-advance-payments.

benefits.name: Carer Payment
benefits.summary: An income support payment if you give constant care to someone with a disability, illness or who is frail aged.
benefits.eligibility_text: Provide constant care to someone with a severe disability, medical condition or who is frail aged; pass income and assets tests.
benefits.value_text: Up to $1,237.70 a fortnight single, $933.00 each for a couple (same as pension rates)
benefits.how_to_claim: Claim online through your Centrelink account with a care needs assessment.
benefits.notes: Carer Payment uses common pension rates (DSS guide 5/1/5/20). Cannot be received at the same time as Age Pension. Services Australia page showed older rates when fetched.

benefits.name: Carer Allowance
benefits.summary: A fortnightly supplement if you give daily care to someone with a disability, medical condition or who is frail aged.
benefits.eligibility_text: You give daily care at home; combined income of you and your partner under $250,000 a year. Can be paid on top of Age Pension.
benefits.value_text: $162.60 a fortnight
benefits.how_to_claim: Claim through your Centrelink online account.
benefits.notes: Not taxable. Income limit from servicesaustralia.gov.au/how-much-carer-allowance-you-can-get.

benefits.name: Carer Supplement
benefits.summary: A yearly lump sum for carers who get Carer Allowance or Carer Payment.
benefits.eligibility_text: Get Carer Allowance, Carer Payment, or DVA Carer Service Pension / Service Pension partner with Carer Allowance, for a period including 1 July.
benefits.value_text: Up to $600 a year
benefits.how_to_claim: Paid automatically.

benefits.name: Carer Gateway
benefits.summary: Free counselling, practical help and support services for unpaid carers.
benefits.eligibility_text: Unpaid carers of someone with a disability, illness, mental health condition or who is frail aged.
benefits.value_text: Free services
benefits.how_to_claim: Call 1800 422 737 or apply online.

benefits.name: Essential Medical Equipment Payment
benefits.summary: A yearly payment to help with extra energy costs of running essential medical equipment or medically needed heating or cooling.
benefits.eligibility_text: You (or the person you care for) hold a PCC, HCC, CSHC or DVA Gold/White card; use essential medical equipment or need extra heating/cooling for a specified condition at home; hold or contribute to the energy account.
benefits.value_text: $203 a year
benefits.how_to_claim: Claim through your Centrelink online account; a medical confirmation may be needed.
benefits.notes: Card list from guides.dss.gov.au 3/15/4/60.

benefits.name: Mobility Allowance
benefits.summary: A fortnightly payment to help with travel costs for people with a disability who cannot use public transport without a lot of help.
benefits.eligibility_text: People with disability or illness who cannot use public transport without substantial help and travel for work, study or volunteering.
benefits.value_text: $122.80 a fortnight standard rate, $171.70 a fortnight higher rate
benefits.how_to_claim: Claim through Centrelink.
benefits.notes: Eligibility not on the fetched rate page; check whether it can be paid alongside Age Pension (generally aimed at people below pension age).

benefits.name: Bereavement payments
benefits.summary: When a pensioner's partner dies, the survivor keeps payments for a bereavement period and may get a lump sum.
benefits.eligibility_text: Surviving partner of a pensioner couple; tell Services Australia about the death.
benefits.value_text: Continued payments during the bereavement period and possibly a lump sum; amount depends on circumstances
benefits.how_to_claim: Tell Centrelink about the death as soon as possible.
benefits.notes: Bereavement period length and lump sum amounts not shown on fetched page (see DSS guide 3/1/5/70).

benefits.name: Australian Government Disaster Recovery Payment
benefits.summary: A one-off payment if you are seriously affected by a declared major disaster.
benefits.eligibility_text: Seriously affected by a disaster the Government has activated the payment for.
benefits.value_text: $1,000 per adult, $400 per child
benefits.how_to_claim: Claim online through myGov within the claim period after the disaster.
benefits.notes: One-off; only available for activated disasters.

benefits.name: Crisis Payment
benefits.summary: A one-off payment if you get an income support payment and face a crisis such as family violence or a disaster.
benefits.eligibility_text: Income support recipients in severe financial hardship due to an extreme circumstance.
benefits.value_text: $618.85 single, $466.50 each partnered (per event)
benefits.how_to_claim: Contact Centrelink within 7 days of the event (check rules).
benefits.notes: Rate taken from DVA CLIK 20 Sep 2026 rates table; DSS guide 5/1/6/30 not opened. Claim time limit not verified.

benefits.name: Seniors and Pensioners Tax Offset (SAPTO)
benefits.summary: A tax offset that means many older Australians pay little or no income tax.
benefits.eligibility_text: Receive an eligible Australian Government pension (or are of pension age and eligible but not paid) and rebate income below the cut-out.
benefits.value_text: Up to $2,230 single, $1,602 each for a couple ($2,040 each if separated by illness); cuts out at $52,759 single / $43,810 each couple
benefits.how_to_claim: Claimed automatically in your tax return.
benefits.notes: Reduces tax payable; worth nothing if you pay no tax.

benefits.name: Downsizer super contribution
benefits.summary: Lets you put up to $300,000 from selling your home into super.
benefits.eligibility_text: Age 55+; owned the home 10+ years; sale qualifies for main residence CGT exemption; contribute within 90 days; not used before.
benefits.value_text: Up to $300,000 per person
benefits.how_to_claim: Give the Downsizer contribution form (NAT 75073) to your super fund.
benefits.notes: Not cash; super balance counts in pension assets test once over pension age.

benefits.name: PBS concessional medicines
benefits.summary: Concession card holders pay a much lower price for PBS prescriptions.
benefits.eligibility_text: Hold a Commonwealth concession card.
benefits.value_text: $7.70 per PBS script (general patients pay $25.00)
benefits.how_to_claim: Show your concession card at the pharmacy.
benefits.notes: Saving depends on number of scripts. DVA card coverage of PBS concession assumed from general practice — verify.

benefits.name: PBS Safety Net
benefits.summary: After you spend a set amount on PBS medicines in a year, the rest of your scripts are free (for concession holders).
benefits.eligibility_text: Concession card holders whose family PBS spending reaches the concessional threshold in a calendar year.
benefits.value_text: Free PBS scripts for the rest of the year after $277.20 spent (general threshold $1,748.20)
benefits.how_to_claim: Ask your pharmacy to keep a record or use a Prescription Record Form; apply for a Safety Net card when you reach the threshold.
benefits.notes: health.gov.au PBS Safety Net page blocked to fetching.

benefits.name: Bulk billing incentives (GP visits)
benefits.summary: GPs get extra payments to bulk bill, so many visits cost you nothing.
benefits.eligibility_text: From 1 Nov 2025 incentives cover all Medicare card holders; concession card holders were already covered.
benefits.value_text: No out-of-pocket cost when your GP bulk bills
benefits.how_to_claim: Ask your GP clinic whether it bulk bills all patients.
benefits.notes: Clinic chooses whether to bulk bill; source is a ministerial media release.

benefits.name: Extended Medicare Safety Net (concessional)
benefits.summary: Once your out-of-hospital medical costs pass a lower concession threshold, Medicare pays back more.
benefits.eligibility_text: Commonwealth concession card holders (and families) whose out-of-pocket costs pass the concessional threshold in a calendar year.
benefits.value_text: Higher Medicare rebates after threshold
benefits.how_to_claim: Automatic once registered as a family/individual with Medicare.
benefits.notes: Threshold amount not on fetched page; health.gov.au/servicesaustralia pages blocked.

benefits.name: Hearing Services Program
benefits.summary: Free or subsidised hearing tests and hearing aids for eligible pensioners and veterans.
benefits.eligibility_text: Australian citizens or permanent residents aged 21+ who hold an eligible card or payment; the Commonwealth Seniors Health Card does NOT qualify.
benefits.value_text: Subsidised hearing assessments, devices and maintenance; vouchers valid 5 years
benefits.how_to_claim: Apply online, through a hearing provider, or with a printed form.
benefits.notes: Exact eligible card/payment list was not visible in fetched text; PCC and DVA Gold/White listed from program rules - verify. Maintenance fee not shown.

benefits.name: Continence Aids Payment Scheme (CAPS)
benefits.summary: A yearly payment to help buy continence products if you have permanent and severe incontinence.
benefits.eligibility_text: Permanent and severe incontinence from an eligible condition; must meet all program requirements.
benefits.value_text: $739.40 a year
benefits.how_to_claim: Apply via Medicare online account or app, or paper form with your health professional's section completed.
benefits.notes: Detailed eligibility not shown on fetched page.

benefits.name: Support at Home (aged care at home)
benefits.provider: Department of Health and Aged Care (via My Aged Care)
benefits.summary: Government-funded help at home such as nursing, personal care, cleaning and gardening; full pensioners pay the lowest contributions.
benefits.eligibility_text: Older people assessed as needing help at home through My Aged Care; contributions depend on pension status and an income/assets assessment.
benefits.value_text: Clinical care free; contributions for independence and everyday living services; lifetime contribution cap $135,318.69
benefits.how_to_claim: Contact My Aged Care to arrange an assessment.
benefits.notes: Exact contribution percentages not on fetched page; aged_65 is the general entry age (50 for First Nations) - not stated on this page.

benefits.name: Commonwealth Home Support Programme (CHSP)
benefits.provider: Department of Health and Aged Care (via My Aged Care)
benefits.summary: Low-cost entry-level help at home such as meals, transport, cleaning and home maintenance.
benefits.eligibility_text: Older people assessed as eligible for CHSP services; pay a contribution based on ability to pay.
benefits.value_text: You pay only a contribution, never the full cost; hardship policies apply
benefits.how_to_claim: Contact My Aged Care for an assessment, then agree fees with a provider.
benefits.notes: Age criterion not stated on fetched page.

benefits.name: Concession stamps
benefits.summary: Buy up to 75 discounted stamps a year for 60c each.
benefits.eligibility_text: Holders of a Pensioner Concession Card, Health Care Card, Commonwealth Seniors Health Card, DVA card or Veterans' Repatriation Health Card.
benefits.value_text: 60c per stamp instead of $1.85, up to 75 a year
benefits.how_to_claim: Fill in the MyPost Concession account form and take it with your card to a Post Office; then show your MyPost Concession card to buy.
benefits.notes: Max annual value calculated as 75 x ($1.85 - $0.60).

benefits.name: No Interest Loan Scheme (NILS)
benefits.provider: Good Shepherd, funded by Department of Social Services
benefits.summary: Interest-free, fee-free loans for essentials like appliances, car repairs or medical costs.
benefits.eligibility_text: Age 18+ and hold a Health Care or Pension card, or income under $70,000 single / $100,000 with partner or dependants, or experienced family violence in last 10 years.
benefits.value_text: Up to $2,000 for essentials, $5,000 for vehicles, $3,000 for disaster relief or rental bonds
benefits.how_to_claim: Use the eligibility checker or find a local provider at nils.com.au.
benefits.notes: Loan, must be repaid.

benefits.name: Service Pension (DVA)
benefits.summary: An income support pension for eligible veterans and their partners, paid at the same rate as Age Pension.
benefits.eligibility_text: Eligible veterans with qualifying service (and partners) who meet age and income/assets tests.
benefits.value_text: Up to $1,237.70 a fortnight single, $933.00 each for a couple
benefits.how_to_claim: Claim through DVA (MyService).
benefits.notes: Eligibility details not on fetched page (DVA service pension page blocked to fetching).

benefits.name: Veterans' Supplement
benefits.summary: A small fortnightly supplement for some veterans and war widows who do not get an income support payment.
benefits.eligibility_text: High rate: Gold Card holders on certain disability compensation payments without income support; low rate: certain war widows, White/Orange card holders without income support.
benefits.value_text: Low $7.00, high $14.00 a fortnight
benefits.how_to_claim: Paid automatically by DVA.
benefits.notes: Eligibility from clik.dva.gov.au/node/16577. Rate may have changed 20 Sep 2026.

benefits.name: War Widow(er)'s Pension
benefits.summary: A pension for widows and widowers of veterans whose death was war-caused (existing recipients).
benefits.eligibility_text: Existing recipients; closed to new claims under the VEA from 1 July 2026.
benefits.value_text: $1,223.40 a fortnight (incl. Energy Supplement)
benefits.how_to_claim: Existing recipients paid automatically.
benefits.notes: VEA closed to new claims 1 Jul 2026; new claims under MRCA - check. Rate may have changed 20 Sep 2026.

benefits.name: DVA funeral benefit
benefits.summary: Help with funeral costs for eligible veterans.
benefits.eligibility_text: Eligible veterans' estates/family as set by DVA.
benefits.value_text: Up to $2,000
benefits.how_to_claim: Claim through DVA.
benefits.notes: One-off. Eligibility rules not on fetched page.
